standard.title: Analyse Different and Contested Historical Interpretations
standard.description: analyse different and contested historical interpretations
standard.prior_knowledge: In Year 7 students explained historical interpretations about significant events, individuals and groups (AC9HH7S07). In Year 8 they continued with explanation (AC9HH8S07). Y9 lifts the demand to analysis — students must now not only identify and explain different interpretations but analyse how and why they differ, including how interpretations change over time as new sources are discovered.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students analyse different and contested historical interpretations, examining how and why interpretations differ and change over time.

nodes.label: Identifying and comparing historical interpretations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and compare different historical interpretations of an event, individual, group, or period, explaining the specific claims each interpretation makes.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two different historical interpretations of the same event or period and explain how they differ.
nodes.typical_width: Explore debates about the historical period or topic being studied; compare similarities and differences in historians' views — about colonial society, the Anzac legend, conscription debates, the Boxer Rebellion, the Industrial Revolution; identify the specific claims being made and the types of evidence used to support each interpretation.
wider: Investigate the same historical event through interpretations from three different time periods — examining how the interpretation of Gallipoli, the Boxer Rebellion, or the Industrial Revolution changed across the 20th century

Compare two directly opposing historical interpretations of the same phenomenon (e.g. the Anzac legend as genuine national identity vs manufactured myth) — constructing a structured analysis of the evidence and reasoning each uses

Examine how a change in dominant social values (e.g. toward recognition of First Nations history) has produced new historical interpretations — analysing the relationship between social context and historical scholarship

response_modes.reason: Comparing interpretations across multiple topics (not just WWI) builds the capacity to recognise contested interpretation as a general feature of historical knowledge — not just a feature of one politically sensitive area.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two different historical interpretations of the same event or period, explaining the specific claims each makes
Compares the interpretations — identifying at least one point of agreement and one point of significant difference

nodes.label: Analysing how and why interpretations change
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse how historians have changed their interpretations of events over time, examining why interpretations change as new sources are discovered, social values shift, or new analytical frameworks emerge.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain one reason why a historical interpretation of an event has changed over time.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse how historians have changed their interpretations over time — explaining the role of new source discoveries, changing social and political contexts, evolving historiographical methods, and decolonisation in producing new interpretations; apply this analysis to a specific historical debate from the topics being studied.
wider: Trace the historiography of one contested topic across three or more decades — mapping how interpretations shifted, what drove the shifts, and what this reveals about the relationship between historical scholarship and its social context

Examine a specific case where new evidence changed historical interpretation (e.g. the discovery of massacre sites in Australian frontier history, or declassified government documents about WWI) — assessing how evidence and interpretation interact

Compare the historiography of the same event in two different national traditions (e.g. how the Boxer Rebellion is interpreted in Chinese vs Western scholarship) — examining how national context shapes historical interpretation

response_modes.reason: Applying interpretation change analysis across different topics — Australian colonial history, WWI, Asian history — builds the analytical capacity as a general skill applicable across historical subjects.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Understanding why historical interpretations change is one of the most sophisticated insights in historical thinking — it requires students to understand history not as a fixed body of facts but as an ongoing, contested interpretive practice. Practising this across multiple contexts builds genuine historical literacy.
success_criteria: Analyses how at least one historical interpretation has changed over time, explaining at least one reason for the change
Identifies at least one factor (new sources, changed values, new analytical frameworks) that drove a change in historical interpretation
